turns.response_html:
Adaptogens are non-toxic plants, such as herbs and roots, that help the body resist physical, chemical, and biological stressors. They work by modulating the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis to maintain homeostasis.

How They Work

Unlike substances that serve a specific targeted function, adaptogens offer a "nonspecific" response. They help the body "adapt" by:

  • Stablizing physiological processes.
  • Reducing cortisol levels during spikes.
  • Boosting energy during periods of fatigue.

Common Examples

PlantPrimary Use
AshwagandhaReducing stress and anxiety.
Rhodiola RoseaCombating burnout and mental fatigue.
Holy BasilImproving focus and lowering inflammation.
Panax GinsengEnhancing immune function and stamina.

[!NOTE] While these are natural supplements, they can interact with medications. It is best to consult a healthcare provider before adding them to a daily routine.

turns.prompt_text: what are some examples of adaptogens
turns.response_html:
Common examples include:

  • Ashwagandha: Reduces cortisol and stress.
  • Rhodiola: Combats fatigue and mental burnout.
  • Holy Basil: Lowers inflammation and supports focus.
  • Panax Ginseng: Boosts stamina and immune health.
  • Reishi Mushroom: Promotes relaxation and sleep quality.
  • Cordyceps: Increases physical energy and oxygen utilization.

No, lavender is not considered an adaptogen. While it is a popular nervine used for relaxation and calming the nervous system, it does not meet the specific criteria of helping the body adapt to metabolic stress via the HPA axis.
